$comment: Inline-asm P5 (D-LANG-GNU-EXTENDED-INLINE-ASM-UNSUPPORTED / D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-OPERANDS): the FIRST runnable witness that a GNU EXTENDED `__asm__` with real operand constraints reaches BYTES. Its sibling `c_inline_asm` covers only the EMPTY template, and an empty template is exactly the shape an expander that emits ZERO instructions passes — so that example says nothing about codegen and this one has to. ★★ THE EXIT CODE IS STRUCTURE-DEPENDENT, NEVER VALUE-DEPENDENT: the x86_64 arm reads the time-stamp counter twice through sqlite `src/hwtime.h`'s own construct (`"rdtsc" : "=a"(lo), "=d"(hi)` — two register-PINNED outputs that must be materialised out of eax/edx) and asserts only MONOTONE-OR-EQUAL, the one property a counter has that does not depend on what it returns. The aarch64 arm holds eight call-derived values live across a template that overwrites the eight registers the allocator actually assigns, declared through the block's clobber list. ★★★ THE aarch64 ARM IS A TRUE NEGATIVE MISCOMPILE PIN AND WAS MEASURED AS ONE: with the clobber list deleted and everything else byte-identical, the `release` arm returns 0 instead of 52. DEBUG DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE (locals are memory-resident before mem2reg) — which is why the `release` arm below is mandatory rather than decorative, and why a future edit must never 'simplify' this example down to its baseline arm. ⚠ The clobbered register list names x21..x28 deliberately: this allocator assigns from the HIGH end, so clobbering x0..x2 is vacuous (measured — the mutant stays green). A clobber pin must name the registers the allocator would otherwise use. ⚠ WHY THERE IS NO `mrs %0, cntvct_el0` ARM: ✔MEASURED 2026-08-15 that NEITHER shipped dialect declares the `%N` operand placeholder — `asm-x86_64-att.lang.json` spells a register `[RegisterSigil, Identifier]` so `%0` lexes as sigil + IntLiteral and matches no operand form, and `asm-arm64-gas.lang.json` is sigil-less with `%` bound to `TypeSigil`. Until a dialect declares the placeholder, an aarch64 asm OUTPUT is unreachable (AArch64 has no register-pinning constraint letter the way x86 has "a"/"d"), so the counter-read half of `hwtime.h` is x86_64-only in this build.
